title: Ground-truth audit of ten public document-AI benchmarks

verdict_scale.present: the answer key holds the property in the sense of the rule
verdict_scale.partial: the key holds part of it, incidentally, implicitly or only for some fields or documents
verdict_scale.absent: the key does not hold it

properties.name: per-field keys
properties.rule: present: each answer is stored under a named field from a fixed schema. partial: answers are keyed, but to free text (a printed label or a question) rather than a fixed set of named fields. absent: no field-level answers (page transcription, layout or table structure only).

properties.name: explicit empties
properties.rule: present: for each document the key states which fields were asked and which have no value (explicitly, or by a documented rule that an asked field left out of the key means 'no value'), so a value returned for an empty field is a countable false positive. partial: emptiness is only implied by omission from a closed field set (sometimes enforced by the scorer), or recorded only as empty table cells. absent: empty fields cannot be told apart from unannotated ones, or the scored split has no empty field at all.

properties.name: canonical beside printed
properties.rule: present: the key stores both the printed form and a normalised (canonical) value. partial: the key stores the canonical value only (the printed form stays in the page or its OCR text, not beside it), or only for some fields. absent: the key stores the printed form only.

properties.name: values never printed
properties.rule: present: the key deliberately includes answers the page does not print (inferred, computed or looked up) and marks them. partial: such answers exist but incidentally and unmarked. absent: every answer is printed on the page, either as written or merely reformatted. Document-level classification labels (type, language) are judged under property 12, not here.

properties.name: evidence locations
properties.rule: present: every answer (or every annotated element, for parsing corpora) carries its position (box or polygon plus page, or character offsets). partial: positions exist for text lines but are not linked to the answers. absent: no positions.

properties.name: derivability flags
properties.rule: present: the key marks whether a missing value can be derived from other values. partial: some derived values are marked. absent: nothing in the schema records derivability.

properties.name: planted traps with controls
properties.rule: present: the corpus plants known defects and pairs them with matched clean controls, and the key says which is which. partial: planted defects without controls, or controls without a key. absent: natural documents only.

properties.name: declared difficulty
properties.rule: present: every document (or page) carries declared difficulty labels or a declared hard subset. partial: per-document attributes that are known difficulty factors, or per-document membership in a harder evaluation condition (unseen layout or template), without a grade. absent: nothing per document.

properties.name: instruction ground truth
properties.paper_wording: instruction ground truth (also called rule ground truth)
properties.rule: present: correct outputs under written customer rules, with an untouched baseline. absent: no rules.

properties.name: payload keys
properties.rule: present: decoded barcode or QR contents are stored. absent: no encoded-content field.

properties.name: line-item / table row structure
properties.rule: present: the key groups values into rows or line items. partial: tables exist only as unstructured text. absent: no row structure.

properties.name: document type labels
properties.rule: present: each document carries a type label from a set of more than one type. partial: type implied only by sub-corpus or file name. absent: single-type corpus with no label, or no label.

properties.name: multi-document segmentation boundaries
properties.rule: present: files holding several documents carry the boundaries. absent: one document per file, or multi-document files removed.

properties.name: entity resolution targets
properties.rule: present: printed names are linked to entries in a master list or registry that contains plausible wrong candidates. partial: the key carries a registry identifier for the real entity, sourced from the registry, but no candidate list. absent: names stored only as printed.

properties.name: repeatability needs (documents only)
properties.rule: present: the documents themselves are distributed, so the same document can be submitted twice and the outputs compared; no answer key is needed. absent: documents not available.

benchmarks.name: SROIE
benchmarks.what_was_downloaded: Answer keys and line transcriptions only (no images): train/entities, test/entities, train/box, test/box from the Losyash/SROIE-datasetv2 mirror (626 train + 347 test receipts). Cross-checked against the 626 raw organiser key files in zzzDavid/ICDAR-2019-SROIE data/key (same keysets, same two gaps) and against the 347 test answers of the Hugging Face copy rth/sroie-2019-v2 (identical). Competition paper text (arXiv 2103.10213).

benchmarks.name: CORD
benchmarks.what_was_downloaded: ground_truth column of the test (100) and validation (100) splits of naver-clova-ix/cord-v2 through the Hugging Face rows API, image column dropped. The train split (800) could not be fetched: the rows API returned HTTP 500 for every train request. CORD README (class table).

benchmarks.name: FUNSD

benchmarks.what_was_downloaded: The full annotation file OmniDocBench.json (42,208,096 bytes, SHA-256 a45cd84b04ad8b793e775089640e6b681209abea33ead54c1828ddca35fae496) and the dataset README; no images.

benchmarks.what_was_downloaded: README, config, expected.tsv for train and dev-0, expected-original.tsv for train, and in.tsv.xz (document text from four OCR tools) for train, dev-0 and test-A, by sparse git checkout; of the 726 PDFs in documents/ only the two behind the computed terms were downloaded. benchmarks.name: Kleister Charity
benchmarks.what_was_downloaded: README, config, expected.tsv for train and dev-0, expected-original.tsv for train, dev-0 in.tsv.xz, the two git-annex fetch scripts, by sparse git checkout; one PDF (the report behind dev-0 line 10, 4,781,158 bytes) fetched from the public S3 annex to check one answer against the page. benchmarks.name: RD-TableBench
benchmarks.what_was_downloaded: Only the 1,000 ground-truth HTML files and providers/scores.csv, read out of the 449,578,580-byte rd-tablebench.zip with HTTP range requests (about 3.6 MB transferred for the ground truth), so the PDFs and images were never downloaded; the grading code README.

cells.evidence: Every key file holds exactly four named fields, company, date, address and total (for example test file X00016469670, lines 2 to 5).

The schema is closed (all 973 key files use only company, date, address, total), but the scored test split has no empty field to invent into: 347 of 347 test keys fill all four (0 of 1,388 cells empty), and a second, independent copy of the test answers (Hugging Face rth/sroie-2019-v2) agrees on all 347. Train has 2 gaps recorded two different ways: X51005663280 omits address (the receipt prints none); X51005433522 stores total as an empty string although the receipt prints a net total (line 21 of its box file).

Values are stored as printed: dates in 17 different shapes (day, month and year in several orders, with slashes, hyphens, dots, spaces or no separator, and months in figures or in letters), totals as printed (with or without a currency sign or code). No canonical value is stored beside them. Only 8 of 1,945 date and total values are stored reformatted instead of as printed (for example train file X51005447850, whose date is stored without the separators the receipt prints), which is annotator variation, not a convention.

All four fields are printed fields: the date is found word for word on one printed line for 965 of 973 receipts and the total for 969 of 972 non-empty totals; of the other 11, 8 are reformatted printed values and 3 disagree with the page (for example test file X51005442322, whose key and receipt give different years); none is inferred.

Box files give a quadrilateral for every printed text line, but the four answers are not linked to boxes; they can only be located by string search, and key and box disagree in places (test file X00016469670: one character of the address differs between key line 4 and box line 7).
Key files contain only company, date, address, total; nothing records derivability.
Real receipts only; no planted defects, no controls, no field that could mark one.
No per-receipt attribute of any kind in key or box files.
Fixed four-field extraction; no rules or rule outputs.
No barcode or QR payload field in the four-field schema.
Header fields only; item lines exist only as unlabelled lines in the box transcription.

source.record: item lines are plain text lines

company is the name as printed (for example train file X00016469612); no registry or master-list identifier.

cells.evidence: gt_parse keys every answer to one of 30 named classes (README class table). Test row 0: menu.nm -TICKET CP, menu.cnt 2, menu.price 60.000, total.total_price 60.000.

No empty value is ever stored (0 empty strings among 2,520 gt_parse values); absence is implied only by a class being left out of a closed 30-class set (sub_total.tax_price appears in at most 91 of 200 receipts).

Values are printed strings only. Test row 0 stores 60.000 for price, item subtotal, subtotal, total and card payment; its 5,411-character annotation contains 60.000 twelve times and 60000 or 60000.00 nowhere. Across 200 receipts, 324 values use a dot as thousands separator and 799 a comma.
Every gt_parse value is assembled from labelled printed words in valid_line; nothing is inferred.
All 4,542 words in valid_line carry a quad (x1..y4) and sit in a line with a category and group_id, so each answer maps to its printed words (test row 0: menu.price word 60.000 at x1 174, y1 410).
Annotation keys are gt_parse, meta, valid_line, roi, repeating_symbol, dontcare; words carry quad, is_key, row_id, text. No derivability marker.
Real receipts only; no planted defects or controls.
meta holds only version, split, image_id, image_size.
No rules or rule outputs.
No payload class among the 30; the only QR in 200 receipts is the printed word QR (validation row 32).
menu is a list of items (nm, cnt, price, sub-items): 472 items over 200 receipts, 115 receipts with more than one; group_id and sub_group_id carry the row grouping.
Receipts only; no type label in meta.
One receipt per image; no boundaries.
No store identity field in the 30 classes; no master list.
Receipt images ship in the dataset's parquet files (image column, dropped by this audit's fetch).

Entities are labelled question, answer, header or other and linked question to answer; the 'key' is the printed question text (for example entity id 22 of testing file 82092117.json), not a named field from a fixed schema.

1,627 of 4,343 question entities have no linked answer, which records many blank form fields (for example entity id 22 of 82092117.json, whose linking list is empty), but unlinked questions also come from table headers, so emptiness is implied, not stated.
Entity text as printed; no normalised value field (entity keys: box, text, label, words, linking, id).
Every entity is a box of printed words.
All 9,743 entities have a box, and all 31,485 words have their own box.
Entity keys are box, text, label, words, linking, id; no derivability field.
Real forms only; no planted defects or controls.
The only document-level key is form.
No rules or rule outputs.
No payload field.
No row or line-item grouping, only question to answer links.
All documents are forms; no type label.
One form per image; no boundaries.
No entity identifiers; names stored as printed.
The 199 form images (149 training, 50 testing PNGs) ship in dataset.zip beside the annotations.
Each field has a fieldtype from 55 classes (paper line 29). The public sample annotation has 11 fields, among them document_id, date_issue, vendor_name, amount_due and customer_id.

No empty marker: a field type absent from a document is simply not listed. The scorer counts unmatched predictions as false positives (FP metric), so omission works as an implicit empty within the closed 55-class set.

text is stored as printed: in the sample, date_issue and date_due hold their dates exactly as printed, in two different shapes; Field has only bbox, page, score, text, fieldtype, line_item_id. Metadata carries a document-level currency label, not a normalised field value.

Fields are annotated as a triplet of location (bounding box and page), field type and text (paper lines 453-455), so every answer is printed. Metadata labels (currency, language, document type) describe the document and are judged under property 12.
bbox and page on 11 of 11 fields and 40 of 40 line-item fields in the sample; the primary metric matches predictions by location.
Field keys are bbox, fieldtype, page, text (plus line_item_id); no derivability marker.
Real documents plus 100k synthetic documents generated from annotated templates (paper line 270), but no planted defects with matched controls.
Each document carries cluster_id, and the evaluator reports 0-shot, few-shot and many-shot layout subsets (README line 110): a declared generalisation condition, not a difficulty grade.
No rules or rule outputs.
No barcode or QR field type; neither word appears in the paper or README.
line_item_id on every LIR field (40 fields in the sample) plus a table grid whose rows are typed header, data, gap, gap-with-text, footer.
metadata.document_type on every document (set in the sample); the paper lists nine invoice-like document types (lines 326-328), selected with a proprietary classifier.
PDF files composed of several documents were split and annotated separately (paper lines 451-452): boundaries were removed during curation, not recorded.
customer_id and vendor_name are stored as printed; no master list.
PDFs are distributed with the annotations once an access token is obtained from docile.rossum.ai (README line 30); one sample PDF is public in the repository.

Annotations are [entity name, mentions] with names fixed by meta.json (registration: file_date, foreign_principle_name, registrant_name, registration_num, signer_name, signer_title; ad-buy: advertiser, agency, contract_num, flight_from, flight_to, gross_amount, product, tv_address, property and line-item fields).

No empty marker, but an entity left out of a document's key counts as absent: the scorer puts any extraction for an entity name not in the ground truth into unmatched extractions, i.e. false positives (benchmark_utils.py lines 489-492). Such cases are common: agency is absent from 358 of 641 ad-buy forms, signer_title from 1,366 of 1,915 registration forms.

Values are stored as printed (dates and prices in many printed shapes; see date_value_shapes_top and price_value_shapes_top). The scorer normalises both sides when scoring (DateMatch, PriceMatch) and even accepts a swapped day and month (match_utils.py line 305), but no canonical value is stored.
Every mention carries a box and a character span into the OCR text, so every answer is printed.

Every mention has [page, x1, y1, x2, y2] plus character offsets (10,051 ad-buy and 8,840 registration top-level mentions), for example the registration_num mention of record 1 of the registration-form annotations, with its box and its character span.
Records are filename, file_path, ocr, annotations; mentions are text, box, spans; no derivability marker.
Real public filings only; no planted defects or controls.

Three tasks of declared rising difficulty (single, mixed, unseen template; README lines 44-58 call the last the hardest), with per-document membership given by the few-shot split files; no per-document grade.
No rules or rule outputs.
No payload entity in either meta.json.

Ad-buy line items are grouped records [channel, program_desc, program_start_date, program_end_date, sub_amount]: 9,163 groups in 636 of 641 ad-buy forms (meta.json pattern line_item). Registration forms have none.

Type is implied by sub-corpus (registration forms vs ad-buy forms); registration sub-types (Amendment, Dissemination Report, Short-Form) appear only in split-file and PDF file names, e.g. 19410222_DLA Piper US LLP_Amendment_Amendment.pdf.
One filing per PDF; no boundaries.
registrant_name and registration_num are annotated from the page with boxes; no link to the FARA register is stored.
Raw PDFs ship in main/pdfs (641 ad-buy, 1,915 registration).
Answers are keyed to free-text questions about a page, not to named fields (for example validation questionId 24580, row_idx 1).
Every question has a non-empty answer (0 of 5,349 validation questions empty); there are no unanswerable questions, so a made-up answer cannot be told apart from a wrong one.

Answers are printed spans with accepted variants; 1,712 of 5,349 questions list variants that differ only in case or punctuation (for example questionId 49168, whose accepted answers write the same times once with a colon and once with a full stop). No canonical form.

Answers are spans of page text. Even the 33 bare yes or no answers are mostly printed words: all 4 pages inspected print the answer word, in a table cell (questionIds 57557 and 56784) or as the label of a ticked box (questionIds 1623 and 39139); the other 29 were not inspected.
Row fields are questionId, question, question_types, image, docId, ucsf_document_id, ucsf_document_page_no, answers, data_split; no answer position.
No derivability field (see row fields).
Real archive pages only; no planted defects or controls.

Each question carries question_types (layout 1,981, table/list 1,780, form 1,021, free_text 765, handwritten 319, figure/diagram 265, others 236, Image/Photo 98, Yes/No 28): evidence-type tags such as handwritten, per question, not a difficulty grade.
Questions ask for a span; there are no written rules with expected transformed outputs.
No payload field.
table/list questions are answered with a single string; no row structure.
No document type field; question_types describe the question, not the document.
One page per question (ucsf_document_page_no); no boundaries.
No entity identifiers.
Page images are distributed (image column). Test answers are withheld (600 of 600 sampled test rows have answers null), which does not matter for repeatability.
Ground truth is page parsing: 32,798 layout elements with category_type (text_block 16,520, title 4,441, table 665, ...) and text, LaTeX or HTML; no named fields.
No fields; empty table cells are recorded as empty in the table HTML (3,759 of 43,771 cells in 665 tables), so text invented into a blank cell is detectable.
Text as printed; LaTeX for formulas and HTML for tables are markup of the printed content, not normalised values.
Every element transcribes what is on the page.
All 32,798 layout elements carry a poly (four corners) and a reading order; spans carry boxes too. Positions are for blocks and spans, not for field values.
Element keys are category_type, poly, ignore, order, anno_id, attribute, text, latex, html, table_edit_status, merge_list; no derivability marker.
The 296 hard pages are selected hard pages, not planted defects with matched controls.

Every page carries page_attribute.special_issue (e.g. fuzzy_scan 30 pages, watermark 73 plus with_watermark 24, geometric_deformation 13, colorful_backgroud 266) and a subset, with 296 pages declared hard (equation_hard 100, layout_hard 99, table_hard 97). First table_hard page: page-c7792da7-4167-4f5c-a7ca-ec0f8833f83b.png.
No rules or rule outputs.
No barcode or QR category among the 28 category types; one page mentions a QR code in a text block only (record 143, page-0b772bee-71ec-4d4a-a406-d7691b1a6e86.png, element box_id_3).
665 tables with HTML ground truth (7,353 tr rows) and LaTeX: table structure for parsing, not business line items.

page_attribute.data_source on all 1,651 pages: book 276, PPT2PDF 253, academic_literature 215, exam_paper 193, colorful_textbook 159, newspaper 151, magazine 149, research_report 132, note 118, historical_document 5.

expected.tsv stores key=value pairs for effective_date, jurisdiction, party and term (for example dev-0 line 1, which holds all four keys, party twice).

Each document's input lists the keys asked (in.tsv column 2, e.g. effective_date jurisdiction party term) and README line 128 says decoy keys are left out of expected.tsv rather than given an empty value. dev-0: 61 asked keys have no value across 48 of 83 documents (term 41, effective_date 15, jurisdiction 5); train: 218 across 160 of 254.

Canonical value only, the printed form is not stored beside it. dev-0 record 1: the effective date, the term and the jurisdiction are written out in words on the page and stored in normalised form (an ISO date, a number with a unit, a place name joined by underscores). All 62 dev dates are ISO and none is printed that way (README lines 153-161).

Incidental and unmarked: some terms are computed from printed dates. train line 196: a term in months, computed from a printed start date and end date (the word month appears nowhere in the PDF's text); train line 15: a term in days, computed the same way; train line 47: a term in years, from an anniversary named in words. 11 of 82 train terms are not printed as a number and unit.
expected.tsv holds key=value only; README line 9 says the task is not named-entity recognition and that where the information sits on the page does not matter.
Nothing marks which answers are derived, although some are (see property 4).

Eight keys: address__post_town, address__postcode, address__street_line, charity_name, charity_number, income_annually_in_british_pounds, report_date, spending_annually_in_british_pounds (dev-0 line 2).

All 440 dev documents are asked all eight keys (in.tsv column 2); 97 asked keys have no value across 66 documents (street_line 50, post_town 18, postcode 14, income 6, spending 6, charity_number 3), e.g. dev-0 line 1 has no income, spending or street. README lines 19-21 describe these decoy keys, which must be left without a value.

Canonical value only. dev-0 line 2: the income is stored as a full amount in pounds where the statement of financial activities prints it in thousands under a thousands heading (the report text also states the full amount), and the report date is stored as an ISO date where the page writes it out in words. 430 of 434 dev income values are not printed in their stored form (README lines 181-202).

Incidental and unmarked: answers were taken from the Charity Commission register (paper lines 278-280), and 9 of 437 dev charity numbers appear in none of the four text layers. dev-0 line 10: the stored charity number appears nowhere in the document, although its 39-page PDF has a text layer on every page and not even the number's first three digits occur in it. The paper (lines 555-556) adds that about 5% of money values need their scale (thousands, millions) inferred.
